insights.insight: The protocol has cryptographically verified 12,411 purchase events across physical retail, dining, fuel, warehouse, and SaaS — each one a confirmed transaction, not a behavioral inference. At $996K in verified GMV, the data asset is approaching a threshold that signals institutional-grade sample depth for brand measurement.

With $3,996 remaining and the last single heartbeat adding $2,055, the $1M milestone clears within the next 1-2 data cycles — making this the first measurable proof point that verified-receipt commerce data can accumulate at meaningful scale outside lab conditions.

insights.topic: Velocity deceleration with early stabilization signal
insights.insight: Week-over-week purchase velocity fell from a peak of 1.241x on April 12 to a trough of 0.819x on April 17 morning — the sharpest single-cycle drop recorded — but the April 17 evening reading shows both velocity (0.855x) and acceleration (1.013x) moving upward simultaneously for the first time since the decline began. One more confirming heartbeat is needed before treating this as a genuine floor.

The network does not expand linearly — it expands in discrete 7-CBSA bursts, with three consecutive identical-magnitude pulses now confirmed across separate heartbeats. For brands planning regional or DMA-level campaigns, this pulse-then-consolidate pattern means coverage gaps are temporary and predictable, not structural.

insights.topic: SaaS subscriptions entered the receipt graph
insights.insight: On April 9, digital SaaS subscriptions appeared as a verified receipt category for the first time, extending the signal set beyond physical retail. For CMOs targeting software buyers or subscription-economy consumers, this marks the first evidence that the protocol captures non-physical commerce intent at the transaction level.

insights.topic: 7-day GMV recovering from a window artifact, not demand collapse
insights.insight: The 7-day GMV dipped to $105K before recovering to $117K — the trough was caused by high-volume April 10 receipts rolling out of the trailing window simultaneously, a mechanical artifact rather than a drop in submission activity. Brands using this data for weekly trend analysis should account for cohort-driven window distortions when interpreting short-term GMV movements.
